title: Goyal pitches India as global trade hub, eyes 75-80% of world economy - The Times of India
summary:
Headline:
India building free-trade network to cover up to 75-80% of world economies, says Piyush Goyal

Source:
The Times of India

Published:
Sat, 03 Oct 2026 06:41:00 GMT

Summary:
Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal told a Chicago audience that India is expanding its free trade agreements and is building a network that could cover nearly 75-80 per cent of the world's economies. He said pre-2014 FTAs covered about $10 trillion in GDP, while 31 newer agreements covered about $60 trillion and another six to eight negotiations cover about $15 trillion. Goyal urged American and Indian-American entrepreneurs to participate as India seeks to grow from a $4 trillion economy to $30 trillion by 2047 and highlighted changes in manufacturing, infrastructure, digital connectivity and defence production. During the visit he met US business leaders, startups and groups to discuss investment, innovation and deeper India-US collaboration, and said government institutions like Invest India could assist investors.

Key Points:
- Goyal said India has negotiated 31 free trade agreements covering about $60 trillion in GDP, adding to $10 trillion covered before 2014, and has another six to eight talks covering about $15 trillion. 
- He invited US and Indian-American entrepreneurs to join India’s growth as it aims to expand from a $4 trillion economy to $30 trillion by 2047. 
- Goyal held meetings with US companies, startups and groups on investment, AI, defence exports and startups, and highlighted government support through bodies like Invest India and engagement with ICAI.

Key Takeaway:
India is actively pursuing broad free-trade agreements and business outreach to deepen global integration and attract US investment as part of a long-term economic expansion plan.

Article:
India is building a network of free trade relationships that could eventually cover nearly 75-80 per cent of the world's economies, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said in Chicago, pitching the country as an expanding base for global trade
